relationships.subject: Chronic compression of the DRG
relationships.evidence_quote: an increase was detected at 7–28 days post-CCD in the levels of TRPV4 mRNA and protein expression in the DRG

relationships.subject: TRPV4
relationships.evidence_quote: the TRPV4 activation-induced Ca2+ influx generates thermal hyperalgesia due to the activation of NO-cGMP-PKG in the CCD model

relationships.subject: TRPV4
relationships.evidence_quote: the TRPV4-mediated Ca2+ influx results in NF-κB activation in the DRG generating neuropathic hyperalgesia in the CCD model

key_findings: Review: TRPV4 antagonists, antisense or knockout reduce mechanical allodynia and heat hyperalgesia in rodent neuropathic pain models, but not cold allodynia.
In the CCD model, TRPV4 Ca2+ influx drives NO-cGMP-PKG and NF-kB signalling in DRG to sustain hyperalgesia.
